title: Backlog
description: An ordered list of work items that the team may deliver, continuously refined and prioritised.

title: Scrum
description: A lightweight framework that helps teams deliver value iteratively through defined roles, events, and artefacts.

title: Three Amigos
description: A collaboration practice where business, development, and testing perspectives align on shared understanding before work begins.

title: Stand-up
description: A short daily meeting where the team synchronises work and identifies blockers.

title: Retrospective
description: A regular team reflection to inspect what went well, what didn’t, and how to improve.

title: User Story
description: A short description of a feature from the user’s perspective, focusing on value rather than implementation.

title: MoSCoW
description: A prioritisation technique that classifies requirements as Must, Should, Could, or Won’t have.

title: Kanban
description: A visual workflow method that helps teams manage and limit work in progress.

title: Epic
description: A large body of work that can be broken down into smaller user stories.

title: BA
description: A Business Analyst helps identify needs, define requirements, and bridge business and technical teams.

title: QA
description: Quality Assurance focuses on preventing defects and ensuring the product meets agreed standards.

title: MVP
description: The Minimum Viable Product is the smallest version of a product that delivers value and enables learning.

title: CI/CD
description: Practices that automate building, testing, and deploying software to improve reliability and speed.

title: Code Review
description: A practice where developers review each other’s code to improve quality and share knowledge.

title: Unit Testing
description: Testing individual units of code to ensure they behave as expected in isolation.

title: Refactoring
description: Improving the internal structure of code without changing its external behaviour.

title: Client Communication
description: Ongoing communication with clients to clarify needs, manage expectations, and build trust.

title: User Acceptance Testing
description: Testing performed by users or stakeholders to confirm the system meets business needs.

title: Pair Programming
description: Two developers working together at one workstation, sharing ideas and responsibility.

title: Agile
description: An approach to software development that values collaboration, feedback, and incremental delivery.

title: User Feedback
description: Information gathered from users to guide improvements and validate assumptions.

title: Story Points
description: A relative measure used by teams to estimate effort and complexity of work items.

title: Project Specification
description: A document describing requirements, constraints, and expectations for a project.

title: Deployment
description: The process of releasing software so it is available for use.

title: Stakeholder
description: Anyone with an interest in or influence over the product, process, or outcome.
